articles.title: A US Air Force veteran who loaned his Iraq war helmet to a Wyoming veterans' post spent 11 days in jail after taking it back; prosecutors later dropped the felony theft case when they could not prove the charge
articles.summary: Discover how a US Air Force veteran faced a wrongful arrest over a combat helmet, the implications of the case, and the eventual dismissal of felony theft charges after supporting evidence emerged.
articles.body: A US Air Force veteran was arrested at an airport and held for 11 days after retrieving a combat helmet he had lent to a veterans' organisation in Wyoming. Prosecutors later dropped the felony theft charge after evidence emerged supporting his claim that the helmet belonged to him.Richard Knapp, 59, was arrested on July 23 at Washington Dulles International Airport while travelling with his wife and three young family members. The family had returned to the United States from the Netherlands to visit his mother and travel to several locations when authorities took him into custody.Speaking to Cowboy State Daily, Knapp said his family had no idea that a warrant had been issued against him. His wife, Nathalie, and the other family members broke down as officers took him away. "We all did," Knapp said, recalling how the family reacted to the arrest.The arrest also raised concerns about his health. Knapp requires anti-rejection medication twice a day after receiving a kidney transplant from his wife three years earlier. He said he was not given the medication while held at the Loudoun Adult Detention Center in Virginia, leaving him worried about the transplanted organ.Eight days after his arrest, Knapp was transferred to Wyoming in a three-day ground journey. He said authorities at the Laramie County jail provided his medication after he arrived in Cheyenne. Describing his experience in custody, he said, "Jail is ... jail." Court records show he was released on August 10 after posting $300 towards a $3,000 bond.How an Iraq war helmet became the subject of a theft caseKnapp served in the US Air Force for 20 years and eight months, including deployments to Iraq and Afghanistan, according to the news outlet. During his service, he worked as a civil engineer and was assigned to a construction battalion. His advanced combat helmet was part of the equipment he used during his deployment to Iraq.After retiring, Knapp became commander of Veterans of Foreign Wars (VFW) Post 4343 in Cheyenne, serving from 2015 to 2016. He allowed the organisation to display his helmet in a glass cabinet alongside other military memorabilia.Greg Anderson, who served as a fellow VFW officer during that period, told Cowboy State Daily that members had voluntarily contributed personal belongings to the display and could reclaim them whenever they wanted."All that stuff in that display case was brought in voluntarily by people," Anderson said. He added that members had the right to take their belongings back at any time.The dispute emerged in September last year, when Knapp returned to the post to collect the helmet. According to an affidavit by Laramie County Sheriff's Deputy Erin Gerhardt-Valois cited by the outlet, surveillance footage showed him opening the display cabinet, removing the helmet and attempting to leave through a side entrance. After finding the door locked, he returned to the room, picked up the helmet and left through the bar area with three companions.The incident was reported to authorities as a theft in October that year. David Stewart, the post's quartermaster, told investigators that the helmet was worth approximately $2,600. Knapp disputed the valuation, telling Cowboy State Daily that it was worth less than $400.The difference in the estimates had legal consequences. Wyoming law sets a $1,000 threshold for felony theft, which carries a maximum prison sentence of 10 years. Theft below that amount is generally treated as a misdemeanour, punishable by up to six months in jail.The Laramie County District Attorney's Office filed a felony charge against Knapp on October 20. A warrant was subsequently issued, but Knapp said he remained unaware of it until his arrest in July 2026.Witness statements helped establish ownershipThe case took a different turn after investigators received statements from people who said they had witnessed Knapp bring the helmet and accompanying goggles to the VFW for display.According to the deputy's report, Knapp's friend Gary Lustgraaf told investigators that the veteran had wanted to retrieve the helmet because the post was undergoing changes and might be closing. Lustgraaf also said Knapp did not intend to take the item to the Netherlands and had left it with him.Anderson and other witnesses also provided accounts supporting Knapp's ownership of the military equipment. Stewart subsequently passed these statements to the investigating deputy on August 4, while Knapp was being transported to Wyoming.Deputy Gerhardt-Valois collected the helmet as evidence and also spoke with Knapp's family about his medical requirements. Her report noted that she contacted jail nursing staff to explain his condition.Laramie County Sheriff Brian Kozak later reviewed the investigation report and told Cowboy State Daily that it provided a complete account of the incident. He also said the deputy had made efforts to assist Knapp during the process.Prosecutors drop felony charge against veteranKnapp hired attorney Sara Lock of Just Criminal Law to represent him. He told Cowboy State Daily that he worked with his lawyer to establish the helmet's actual value and provide information supporting his ownership claim.On September 1 this year Laramie County Deputy District Attorney William Edelman filed a motion seeking dismissal of the case, stating that the prosecution could not meet its burden of proof. Circuit Court Judge Sean Chambers approved the request the following day.The dismissal ended the felony proceedings against Knapp after he had spent 11 days in custody and travelled across the country under extradition arrangements.Although the case was dropped, Knapp said the experience had affected him, particularly given his concerns about his kidney transplant and the time spent in detention. He also said he had no intention of returning to the VFW post."I'm glad I was proven innocent," Knapp told outlet. "I would never do anything like (felony theft). Never."You use AI every day. articles.title: Thief drives stolen car 230km away from Chennai unaware of girl sleeping in rear seat
articles.summary: CHENNAI: A car thief driving a stolen vehicle found something he had not bargained for: A 12-year-old child sleeping in the rear seat.
articles.body: CHENNAI: A car thief driving a stolen vehicle found something he had not bargained for: A 12-year-old child sleeping in the rear seat. While the circumstances under which the girl’s presence inside the car came to light are still unclear, police said the girl managed to escape from the vehicle at Sirkazhi, which is about 230km away from Guduvanchery, a Chennai suburb, from where the vehicle was stolen on Sunday night.The girl managed to speak to autorickshaw drivers at the Sirkazhi new bus stand in Mayiladuthurai district early on Monday morning, but the suspect fled with the vehicle.Police said the girl’s father, a native of Kamuthi in Sivaganga district, was returning to his residence in Guduvanchery with his wife and daughter after visiting his hometown. His daughter was sleeping in the rear seat. During the journey, the family stopped at their cloud kitchen at Vallanchery, near Guduvanchery, to eat. The couple stepped out of the car, leaving their daughter asleep inside. An unidentified man noticed the unattended vehicle that was kept on and drove away with it, apparently unaware of the child’s presence.When the couple returned after 30 minutes, they found both the car and their daughter missing. After searching the surrounding areas, the girl’s father lodged a complaint with Guduvanchery police. Police registered a case and formed three special teams to trace the girl and the vehicle. Police examined CCTV footage from nearby establishments and collected details of vehicles that had passed through the area.Around 4.30am on Monday, the suspect reached the Sirkazhi new bus stand when the child woke up. Noticing the child, he reportedly told the girl that he would buy her tea. When he stepped out of the car, the girl escaped and approached autorickshaw drivers at the bus stand. She narrated the incident to them, but the suspect fled with the vehicle before they could catch him.The drivers immediately took the girl to the Sirkazhi all women police station and handed her over to police. Sirkazhi police alerted their Guduvanchery counterparts and informed the girl’s parents about her rescue.Police said the girl was safely reunited with her family. Police suspect the man stole the car without initially realising that she was sleeping inside. articles.summary: Texas supermarket chain H-E-B turned an ordinary Saturday grocery run into an unexpected windfall for thousands of shoppers.
articles.body: Texas supermarket chain H-E-B turned an ordinary Saturday grocery run into an unexpected windfall for thousands of shoppers. On November 14, the company surprised 10,000 customers across the state with $100 gift cards, covering a total of $1 million in groceries as families prepared for the holiday season, according to H-E-B’s newsroom and reporting by AOL. The giveaway took place at H-E-B stores throughout Texas, including locations in Corpus Christi. Shoppers had no advance warning, and many learned about the surprise only as they reached the checkout line, making the moment feel less like a marketing promotion and more like a small, immediate act of relief.How the giveaway workedH-E-B selected 30 shoppers at random at each participating store. Each selected customer received a $100 gift card as they checked out, bringing the company’s total giveaway to $1 million in a single day.The company did not require shoppers to enter a contest or meet any special condition. The surprise was built directly into the checkout experience, which meant that customers could receive the benefit while paying for groceries they had already chosen.The event impacted shoppers in large and small communities alike with 10,000 gift cards distributed throughout the state. The $100 credit could assist families already struggling with holiday costs with staples, seasonal food, household essentials or a part of a larger grocery bill.A timely gift for people who shopTiming was important. November is a month when household budgets often come under pressure as families plan Thanksgiving meals, holiday travel, gifts and other seasonal costs.A $100 grocery credit does not solve every financial challenge, but it can make an immediate difference. It can reduce the amount a shopper pays out of pocket on a particular trip and provide a little breathing room during an expensive time of year.H-E-B’s decision to give the cards directly to shoppers at checkout also made the benefit tangible. Rather than offering a discount code or a future promotion, the company put money in customers’ hands at the moment they were paying for food.The surprise produced emotional reactions in stores from customers. The other recipients probably experienced the gift differently. Some may have stretched out their weekly grocery budget, some may have put it toward holiday food or everyday necessities. The shared experience, however, was the same: an ordinary errand became a moment of unexpected support.Why H-E-B did itH-E-B has long positioned itself as more than a grocery retailer in Texas. The company’s community focused identity is closely tied to its presence across the state, where it operates hundreds of stores and plays a visible role in local life.The $1 million giveaway fits that approach. Rather than announcing a broad discount, H-E-B created a direct, personal interaction with 10,000 customers, giving each person a specific and immediate benefit.The move also comes as grocery prices and household costs remain a worry for many families. The company framed the giveaway in terms of groceries, connecting its gesture to a basic need rather than a luxury purchase.What communities can expectFor participating stores the event probably made for a memorable day for staff and shoppers. Employees could tell customers about the good news, and shoppers had a chance to score a surprise bonus on a regular trip.The giveaway can also help build customer loyalty. Consumers who feel appreciated by a local business are more likely to come back again, especially if the appreciation feels sincere and not simply a sales tactic.In a larger context the event showed how a fairly simple idea can have a wide reach. By giving $100 to 10,000 people, H-E-B turned a $1 million commitment into thousands of individual moments of relief across Texas.Reminder of local impactThe giveaway was not a major infrastructure project or long term policy solution. It was a one day gesture, but its value lay in its immediacy and its connection to everyday life.The customers who received the cards had real benefit. For the company, it was an opportunity to demonstrate appreciation for the communities that support its stores.The surprise was a reminder that as the holiday season approaches, small acts of generosity have meaningful weight. In this case, H-E-B’s $1 million in groceries reached 10,000 Texas shoppers, one checkout line at a time.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Dhaka denies India set conditions for Hasina’s return
articles.summary: DHAKA: State minister for foreign affairs Shama Obaid Islam on Monday said Bangladesh expects former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, who has been sentenced
articles.body: DHAKA: State minister for foreign affairs Shama Obaid Islam on Monday said Bangladesh expects former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, who has been sentenced to death for crimes against humanity, to be brought back from India under the existing extradition treaty, dismissing reports of possible conditions attached to her return.“This report has no basis. It did not originate from a responsible source within the Indian government. Anyone could publish such a report. Ultimately, a report like this means nothing,” she told reporters at the ministry of foreign affairs, noting that if an official communication were to come from India - specifically from their Ministry of External Affairs or the Indian government itself – they would certainly receive it and provide a response.“Beyond that, we have neither the time nor the inclination to concern ourselves with what is being published elsewhere in India; it is simply not our business,” she said.On the other hand, independent MP Rumeen Farhana has said she could see inconsistencies in statements made by ministers and an adviser to the prime minister regarding the intended return of Hasina.She said the relationship between Bangladesh and India is far broader than just Sheikh Hasina. “The relationship is not confined to this single issue. We do have issues, but we will resolve them through our diplomatic channels. I think we are making this far more important than it needs to be,” she said, noting that Bangladesh currently has many other issues to discuss - the government is engaged in a great deal of work, and there are numerous matters that deserve their attention beyond this.“I would ask: why wouldn’t India make use of the extradition treaty? The treaty exists. Any accused individual - they all fall into the same category. They could all be brought back under the provisions of the extradition treaty. If India were to respond in this regard, it would make things easier for the people of Bangladesh, as well as for the government of Bangladesh,” she told reporters while responding to a question at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.The Ministry of Foreign Affairs has written to India multiple times under the extradition treaty," she said, adding that the Ministries of Law and Home Affairs are examining the legal and technical aspects of the matter.Shama said the government believes Hasina, like any other accused persons, should be brought back under the treaty to serve her sentence.“Simply being a citizen of Bangladesh does not guarantee that you will be issued a Bangladeshi passport – if you are a convicted criminal, if you are implicated in cases involving crimes against humanity,” she said.Responding to reports that India had set two conditions for Hasina's return, including providing her an opportunity to appeal and restarting her trial, the State Minister said the reports have no basis in Bangladesh's laws.“No, not at all. We have had no such conversations with them on this matter,” she said, making it clear that Bangladesh had received no such official proposal from India as reported by BBC Bangla.Shama said Bangladesh-India relations are much broader than the issue of Hasina, stressing that the two neighbouring countries have longstanding ties and several important bilateral issues that need to be addressed through diplomacy.“Bangladesh-India relations are a much bigger deal than Sheikh Hasina,” she said, urging against making the issue appear more important than it needs to be."We have issues. We will deal with the issues through diplomacy," Shama said.However, she said the government cannot ignore Hasina's activities in India if they are aimed at destabilising Bangladesh.On the Bangladesh-India Consular Dialogue, originally scheduled for November 17-18, Shama said the meeting had not been cancelled but deferred to a mutually convenient time.She described reports suggesting that the meeting had been cancelled as misinformation, saying both sides agreed that it would be better to hold the talks later when the respective sides are available.The State Minister also indicated that Bangladesh would host several high-level foreign visits in the coming days, although she did not disclose any names or tentative dates.Asked whether water-sharing issues, particularly the Ganges water issue, were discussed at a meeting with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, Shama said the government could hold extensive discussions with the Prime Minister on a range of issues.She, however, did not directly confirm whether the Ganges water issue was discussed at the meeting.The State Minister said, “We have not forgotten the history of petrol bombs. The acts of arson and destruction that took place in the past were carried out by the Awami League, and the arson and destruction happening now are also being carried out by the Awami League - this is a proven fact. And when such a terrorist group operates from another country - a nation with which we have relations and with which we need to foster stronger ties - then, as the government of Bangladesh, it is certainly our responsibility to address this.”You use AI every day. articles.title: Brazilian Uber driver was stabbed 10 times and left quadriplegic but she doesn't want to leave the country. She begs Australia to let her stay after her student visa expires during hospitalization
articles.summary: A Brazilian woman who was stabbed 10 times and strangled with a seatbelt by a teenage passenger while working as an Uber driver in Australia is appealing
articles.body: A Brazilian woman who was stabbed 10 times and strangled with a seatbelt by a teenage passenger while working as an Uber driver in Australia is appealing to the government to let her remain in the country after her student visa expired while she was fighting for her life in hospital. Giovanna Paola Ramos Muccio, who has lived in Australia since 2016, suffered devastating spinal cord injuries in the September 2025 attack that left her quadriplegic. After spending five months in hospital, she has made significant progress in her recovery but continues to experience pain and physical limitations.Now, she has asked the Australian government to consider her circumstances and provide her with a lawful pathway to permanent residency, saying she does not want to lose the life she spent years building in the country because of a crime committed against her.In a petition titled "Desperately Seeking Support to Stay in Australia – Victim of Crime", launched on Change.org on November 11, Muccio described the attack and the immigration difficulties that followed."My name is Giovanna Paola Ramos Muccio. I survived a violent attack that almost took my life. After everything I have endured, I am asking for one thing: the opportunity to have a future in Australia, the country I have called home since 2016," she wrote.What happened to Giovanna Muccio?The attack took place in September 2025 when Muccio was working as an Uber driver on the Gold Coast in Queensland.According to Australian media reports, she was dropping off a 16-year-old passenger near Westfield Coomera when the teenager allegedly attacked her. He attempted to strangle her with a seatbelt before stabbing her 10 times in the face, neck and back. She was left paralyzed inside her vehicle, with a punctured lung and serious injuries. A passing security guard discovered her several hours later and alerted authorities.Her father and brother travelled from overseas to be with her as she began a long and uncertain recovery.Muccio had been working two jobs, including as an Uber driver and a chef, to finance her visa and build a future in Australia. She had also planned to return to Brazil to visit her family, but the attack put those plans on hold.The teenage passenger was accused of attempted murder, according to Muccio's petition, which says the criminal case now involves attempted murder charges.Student visa expired while she was in hospitalWhile Muccio was undergoing treatment and trying to recover from her injuries, her student visa expired.She said the circumstances that affected her immigration status were beyond her control, as she had never anticipated spending five months in hospital after being attacked while working."While I was in hospital, fighting for my life and trying to recover from my injuries, my immigration circumstances were also affected. My student visa expired while I was hospitalised and receiving treatment," she wrote."I had not planned for this. I did not choose to become a victim of a violent crime. I did not choose to spend five months in hospital or to have my career and independence taken away from me."According to a report by Brazilian publication UOL, Muccio currently has temporary immigration permission that is due to expire on March 27, 2027. She is concerned that the lasting physical consequences of the attack could also affect her ability to meet the medical requirements associated with permanent residency.'I am not asking for special treatment'In her petition, Muccio said she was not demanding an exemption from immigration laws but wanted the government to consider the extraordinary circumstances of her case. "I am not asking for special treatment without consideration of the law. I am asking for my individual circumstances to be recognised with compassion, fairness and humanity," she wrote. She appealed to the Australian government, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke and members of parliament to consider providing her with a fair and lawful pathway to permanent residency."I do not want everything I have worked for since arriving in Australia in 2016 to end because of a crime committed against me," she said. "I survived the attack. I fought to recover. I am rebuilding my life. Now I am asking Australia to give me the chance to continue it here."You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: In 2013, a Canadian teacher's death inspired a charity for children in need; 13 years later, Noelle's Gift has provided more than $5 million, including $259,200 for two school boards in the past year
articles.summary: Noelle's Gift to Children has raised over $5 million to provide essential support for children in need. Discover how this charity continues to impact local schools in Ontario, ensuring students have access to food, clothing, and healthcare.
articles.body: A Canadian kindergarten teacher's death in 2013 led her family and community to establish a charity that has since distributed more than $5 million to support children and families. Thirteen years later, Noelle's Gift to Children has reached another milestone, providing $259,200 to two school boards in the past year to help students access food, clothing, healthcare and other essential items.The latest funding was presented on Thursday to the St. Clair Catholic District School Board and the Lambton Kent District School Board, which serve communities across Chatham-Kent and Sarnia-Lambton in Ontario.The contribution takes the organisation's total donations beyond $5 million since its establishment in memory of Noelle Paquette, who was killed in January 2013.How Noelle's Gift supports children and familiesThe charity works with schools to address needs that can affect a child's ability to participate in education. Its funding supplements the Ontario Student Nutrition Program, helping schools provide breakfast, lunches and snacks to students.It also covers individual requirements that families may struggle to afford, including emergency dental treatment, eyeglasses, winter clothing, school supplies and lice treatment kits.Speaking to Windsor News Today, Lambton Kent District School Board CEO Gary Girardi said the funding allows schools to respond when students need assistance."It's used for direct support to our students in all of our schools, from emergency items to things like specific needs for individual students," Girardi said.He added that the partnership allows support to reach children quickly rather than leaving families to wait for assistance.The organisation also supports Noelle's Gift Closets in almost all schools across the two boards. These spaces provide students with discreet access to necessities such as personal hygiene products, non-perishable food and clean clothing.Why the charity was established in 2013Noelle's Gift to Children was founded after the death of Paquette, a kindergarten teacher remembered by colleagues and families for her generosity towards children.Her mother, Lynn Paquette, helped establish the organisation to continue the work Noelle had carried out during her life, ensuring children had the resources they needed to learn and develop.The charity's support also extends to school nutrition programmes, where rising food costs have made it harder to provide meals and snacks.Speaking to Windsor News Today, Lynn explained why additional funding is necessary, pointing to the limited government contribution towards student nutrition."The government only provides 25 cents per day, per child, and you can't even buy an apple for 25 cents," she said.She added that Noelle's Gift supplements the programme for students in Chatham-Kent and Sarnia-Lambton.School boards credit community support for $5 million milestoneThe organisation's latest contribution has been welcomed by both school boards, which say its assistance helps address growing needs among students and their families.Lisa Demers, CEO of the St. Clair Catholic District School Board, said the charity's work provides more than financial assistance.Its contribution, she said, reassures children and families that support is available when they face difficulties.Girardi also described the partnership as essential to the assistance schools can provide, saying the demand for help in local communities continues to increase.For Lynn Paquette, the $5 million milestone reflects the efforts of people and businesses that have supported the organisation over the years."As much as the school boards are grateful to our organization, we are equally grateful to the communities that continue to support us," she said in the school boards' joint announcement.She credited individual donors, families, businesses, volunteers and community partners with helping the charity continue its work.You use AI every articles.title: Twenty years after Warren Buffett began giving away his fortune, the 96-year-old investor has announced another $5.47 billion gift to four family foundations, taking his giving to those charities past $29 billion
articles.summary: Warren Buffett is speeding up his plans to give away his wealth, announcing a fresh donation of Berkshire Hathaway shares worth around $5.47 billion to
articles.body: Warren Buffett is speeding up his plans to give away his wealth, announcing a fresh donation of Berkshire Hathaway shares worth around $5.47 billion to four charities run by his family. The 96-year-old investor announced the Thanksgiving donation in a statement released by Berkshire Hathaway on Monday, 16 November 2026. The latest gift takes his total donations to the four foundations beyond $29 billion, around 20 years after he first started giving away his fortune. According to Berkshire Hathaway's announcement, Buffett is converting 6,150 Class A shares into 9,225,000 Class B shares to make the donation. Based on Friday's closing price of $592.94 per Class B share, the gift is worth approximately $5.47 billion. The latest donation is more than four times the size of his Thanksgiving gift in 2025. At that time, he converted 1,800 Class A shares into 2.7 million Class B shares, worth around $1.3 billion. Including a separate donation of nearly $6 billion in July, Buffett has now given approximately $11.4 billion to the four family charities in 2026.How the shares are dividedBerkshire Hathaway said in its press release that the 9,225,000 Class B shares would be divided among the four organisations, with different amounts going to each. The Susan Thompson Buffett Foundation, named after his late first wife, will receive the largest share of the donation. It will get 3,690,000 shares, equal to 40 per cent of the total gift. The foundation focuses on reproductive health and rights. The other three foundations, which are overseen by Buffett's children Susie, Howard and Peter, will receive equal amounts. The Sherwood Foundation, the Howard G. Buffett Foundation and the NoVo Foundation will each get 1,845,000 Class B shares. As reported by Insurance Business, each of the three foundations run by his children supports different causes. The Sherwood Foundation provides funding to non-profit organisations in Buffett's home state of Nebraska. The Howard G. Buffett Foundation works on global food security, while the NoVo Foundation supports programmes for women and girls. The Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation was not included in the latest donation. As noted by Morningstar, Buffett skipped his regular contribution to the organisation in July for the first time in 20 years. This followed disclosures about Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates's past connections to Jeffrey Epstein. Buffett had also said in 2024 that the Gates Foundation would not receive any money from his estate after his death.Reflections on kindness and company leadershipBuffett also released a short Thanksgiving letter alongside the donation announcement. It was noticeably shorter than the lengthy message he shared in 2025. In the letter, he spoke about the people who helped shape his career, including investor Ben Graham, Iowa philanthropist Joe Rosenfield and former Capital Cities chief Tom Murphy. "Much of my good fortune has come in the form of people who were kind to me and expected nothing in return. I'm grateful to every one of them," Buffett wrote in the letter. "This Thanksgiving, thank one of those selfless people in your own life. Better yet, be a benefactor for someone else." He also returned to an idea he had shared in his previous Thanksgiving message, comparing kindness with financial returns. "Last Thanksgiving I wrote that kindness is costless but also priceless," Buffett wrote. "A year later, I would only add that it compounds." According to Startup Fortune, he also said that kindness "compounds, and at a better rate than anything Charlie and I ever bought." He was referring to his late business partner, Charlie Munger.The donation comes as Berkshire Hathaway continues its leadership changes. Buffett stepped down as chief executive at the end of 2025, handing the position to Greg Abel. He officially retired as chairman in September 2026 and now holds the title of chairman emeritus. His eldest son, Howard Buffett, has taken over as chairman. In his Monday letter, Buffett also repeated his confidence in the company's new leadership. "You heard plenty from me in September about my confidence in Berkshire. That confidence is as strong as ever," he wrote while addressing shareholders. Berkshire Hathaway chief executive Greg Abel also responded to the donation announcement. In a statement quoted by BigGo Finance, he said: "Warren continues to share his wisdom with us all during this holiday season. His example reflects the kindness he encourages in all of us."A strict deadline for the remaining fortuneDespite giving away more than 60 per cent of his original stake since 2006, Buffett remains Berkshire Hathaway's largest individual shareholder. After the latest donation, he still owns 182,140 Class A shares and 1,162 Class B shares. His remaining holdings are worth more than $160 billion. Buffett repeated in his Thanksgiving message that he has complete trust in his three children. He plans to donate all his remaining Berkshire Hathaway shares to the four foundations run by his family. According to Fortune, Buffett set a firm deadline in July to give away the rest of his holdings "one way or the other by December 31, 2034."The size of the planned future donations has also led to discussions among organisations in Omaha. The Sherwood Foundation already provides a large share of the funding received by charities across Nebraska. Steve Isom, chief operating officer and chief financial officer of non-profit software company Bloomerang, previously told Fortune that the Sherwood Foundation had been working with consultants and carrying out feasibility studies with local organisations. The aim was to understand how much additional funding these groups could receive and use effectively.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: An Illinois man withdrew his dead grandmother's Social Security payments for nearly 10 years while officials believed she was alive; a federal judge sentenced him to 15 months and ordered $107,175 forfeited
articles.summary: An Illinois man was sentenced to 15 months in prison for withdrawing over $107,000 in Social Security payments from his deceased grandmother's account, evading detection for nearly a decade.
articles.body: An Illinois man has been sentenced to 15 months in federal prison after taking more than $107,000 in Social Security payments deposited into his deceased grandmother's bank account over nearly a decade.Jonathan Frank Barner, 55, continued accessing the account and spending the retirement benefits on his personal expenses between May 2013 and April 2023, according to the DOJ. A federal judge also ordered him to forfeit $107,175, representing the proceeds of the offence.US District Judge John Baldalamenti imposed the sentence after Barner pleaded guilty to theft of government money on May 18 this year. US Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe announced the sentencing.How the man continued collecting his grandmother's benefitsCourt documents show that the Social Security Administration continued depositing monthly retirement payments into the grandmother's bank account because officials had not been informed of her death.Barner did not notify the agency about her death. Instead, he repeatedly accessed the account, withdrew the money and used it to cover his own expenses.The arrangement continued for almost 10 years, with the government payments reaching the account until April 2023. The deposits stopped after the Social Security Administration ended the payments and the account was exhausted.According to the Justice Department, Barner took more than $107,000 in government funds during this period.Federal investigation leads to prison sentenceThe Social Security Administration's Office of the Inspector General investigated the case, which was prosecuted by Special Assistant US Attorney Matthew Del Mastro.The court also ordered Barner to forfeit $107,175, covering the money obtained through the scheme. Assistant US Attorney Suzanne Nebesky handled the forfeiture proceedings.DOJ outlines wider fraud enforcement effortsThe Justice Department also highlighted its wider efforts to investigate misuse of federal benefit programmes.On April 7, the department announced the creation of its National Fraud Enforcement Division, tasked with investigating and prosecuting cases involving fraud against the American public.The initiative is part of the administration's broader Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, chaired by Vice President JD Vance. The task force is intended to coordinate efforts across federal agencies to address fraud, waste and abuse involving government benefit programmes.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Congress on Monday constituted screening committees for five states scheduled to hold assembly elections, with party president Mallikarjun
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Congress on Monday constituted screening committees for five states scheduled to hold assembly elections, with party president Mallikarjun Kharge appointing senior leaders to head the panels. Ajay Maken will lead the committee for Uttar Pradesh, while Sirivella Prasad has been named chairperson of the Punjab panel.The committees have also been formed for Uttarakhand, Goa and Manipur. Each panel comprises a chairperson and two other members and will be responsible for the party's screening process ahead of the elections.Who heads the screening panelsFor Uttar Pradesh, Maken will be joined by Aslam Shaikh and B V Srinivas. The Punjab committee will be headed by Sirivella Prasad, with Sachin Sawant and Nivedith Alva as members.In Uttarakhand, Deepa Dasmunsi will chair the panel, which includes Anil Chaudhary and Pal Bhai Ambaliya. KJ George will head the Goa committee, with Satej D Patil and Shafi Parambil as members.For Manipur, B M Sandeep has been appointed chairperson. articles.title: Trump claims US intercepted 99.99% of Iranian missiles and drones, hits out at CBS '60 Minutes' report
articles.summary: President Trump asserts that the US military has intercepted nearly all Iranian missile and drone attacks since the start of the conflict, challenging CBS News for its coverage of Iranian threats to American forces.
articles.body: US President Donald Trump has claimed that American forces intercepted all Iranian drones and ballistic missiles launched since the start of the war, accusing CBS News' 60 Minutes of overlooking the effectiveness of US military defences in its latest investigation.In a post on Truth Social on Monday, Trump said Iran had launched between 8,000 and 9,000 one-way attack drones since Operation Epic Fury began on February 28. He claimed only two had penetrated US defences and caused American fatalities, in attacks on Kuwait and Saudi Arabia on the first day of the conflict.Trump also said Tehran had fired approximately 2,000 ballistic missiles, of which only one had penetrated US defences and resulted in American deaths in Jordan.“99.99% of Iranian missiles and drones have been shot down or, in any event, not caused U.S. deaths,” Trump wrote, describing the performance of US Central Command (CENTCOM) as “historically effective”.He further criticised the television programme for not including the figures in its coverage of Iranian attacks on American military installations.“The new people running 60 Minutes are even worse than their predecessors,” Trump wrote, arguing that the programme had not correctly presented the findings of its investigation.His remarks came after a CBS 60 Minutes investigation found that Iranian attacks had hit at least 31 US military and diplomatic sites across eight countries, damaging hundreds of buildings and structures. The investigation used satellite imagery, videos and interviews with military personnel and families of service members killed in the conflict.One of the attacks examined was the March 1 Iranian drone strike on a US Army command post at Port Shuaiba in Kuwait, which killed six American soldiers.CBC News also interviewed Army Maj. Stephen Ramsbottom, who survived the March 1 drone strike in Kuwait, alleged that the Pentagon ignored warnings about inadequate protection at the command post. He said military officials failed to provide a requested counter-drone system before the attack.Ramsbottom has since submitted a whistleblower complaint to congressional committees seeking an investigation into the security arrangements at the command post.You use AI every day. articles.summary: An American professional basketball player has been arrested in Nigeria after authorities allegedly found 33.95kg of cannabis in two suitcases he
articles.body: An American professional basketball player has been arrested in Nigeria after authorities allegedly found 33.95kg of cannabis in two suitcases he abandoned at Lagos' main international airport.The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) identified the suspect as Greene Da'monte Khiree, 28, from Savannah, Georgia. According to the BBC, he arrived at Murtala Muhammed International Airport on November 11 from Thailand via Dubai on an Emirates flight.The agency said Khiree was arrested after airport officials noticed him abandoning two checked-in bags bearing his name and attempting to leave with his carry-on luggage. He was subsequently apprehended in the airport car park.An examination of the suitcases allegedly uncovered 32 packages of cannabis, known as "Loud", a potent strain of the drug, weighing a total of 33.95kg. Officers also recovered a tracking device from the bags, the agency said.According to the NDLEA, Khiree told investigators that he had been living and playing professional basketball in Thailand since October 2025 and had travelled to Nigeria for a holiday to build networks for his career.The agency said a forensic examination of his mobile phone revealed information suggesting he knew about and was involved in the alleged drug trafficking operation.The basketball player has not publicly commented on the allegations.The International Basketball Federation (FIBA) lists a player named Damonte Greene, whose most recent appearance was at the Phuket Elite Cup in Thailand on September 26.Greene previously played for Reinhardt University's basketball team in the US during the 2017-18 season before moving to South Georgia Technical College. He later became the leading scorer for the Georgia Bombers semi-professional team during the 2023-24 season before moving to Thailand.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient.
